## Where the rules live

Source of text: `packages/runtime/src/instructions/claude-5.5/`
- Core (in every non-root context): `root/identity.md`, `root/delegating.md`, `root/dispatch.md`, `root/task-list.md`. Listed in `root-core.ts:11-16`; joined at `root-core.ts:22-24`.
- Full root prompt, built by `packages/integrations/claude/src/agents.ts:457-469` (`rootAgent`, model opus). Section order is `ROOT_SECTIONS` at `agents.ts:115-130`. Output is `packages/integrations/claude/dist/agents/holyagent.md`.
- Session reminder (5 bullets, injected last at every session start): `session-reminder.md:1-10`. Test asserts exactly 5 bullets (`sessioncontext.test.ts:197`).
- Behavior requirements: `packages/runtime/src/instructions/requirements.md`. Each id maps to a section and a phrase in `REQUIREMENT_SECTIONS` (`agents.ts:208-353`), and `plugin.test.ts:328-375` fails when a requirement lacks an implementing phrase.
- Specialist text: `specialist/*.md`, with per-role files under `roles/<agent>/` (`agents.ts:180-199`).
- Generated copies in `dist/`: `dist/agents/holyagent.md`, and `dist/scripts/holyagent.js` (ROOT_CORE at :11748, reminder at :12447, ROOT_TAKEOVER at :12458). Rebuild with `mise run build` after source edits.

Tool grant for the root: `agents.ts:73-86` (ROOT_BUILTINS) keeps Bash, Read, Task* and Workflow. `denylist` (`agents.ts:92-95`) denies everything else built in, so Write and Edit are denied. Bash is not denied. Frontmatter enforcement is inferred, not run.

## The six observed failures

1. Root writes files via Bash
- Rule text: `root/delegating.md:3` ("your Bash is for the holyagent CLI, Git and gh"), and `requirements.md:7` and `:18` (R-ROLE, R-DELEGATE). `session-reminder.md:1` says "the main thread does not edit files". `sessioncontext.ts:23` (ROOT_TAKEOVER) says "never implementing in the main thread".
- Gap: no line names Bash file writes (heredoc, redirection, `python -c`, `sed -i`). `delegating.md:3` permits Bash for the CLI, Git and gh, which is the opening a shell write uses. The only write-related hook (`vcs-reminder`, `hook.ts:291-303`) fires only on `git commit|push`, so file writes via Bash are unguarded.
- Ambiguity: "Read only what a decision needs" (`delegating.md:3`) has no definition.

2. Work before the Intent
- Rule text: `assignments.md:3` ("The Intent states a one-sentence objective..."), `requirements.md:7` (R-ROLE, "running all work through an Intent and Assignments"), `sessioncontext.ts:23`, `session-reminder.md:1`.
- Gap: no requirement or section says "create the Intent before any work". The only Intent-first text is a description of its contents. Session start injects status only (`sessioncontext.ts:141-172`), and nothing creates or checks an Intent. Strongest gap of the six.

3. No task list when task tools are missing
- Rule text: `task-list.md:3` ("Create the task list first (TaskCreate/TaskUpdate, or update_plan on desktop)"), `session-reminder.md:5` ("Load the task-list tool if it is deferred"), `requirements.md:10` (R-TASKLIST), `agents.ts:213` (phrase check).
- Gap: no fallback for when neither tool exists. `ROOT_BUILTINS` (`agents.ts:80-83`) lists TaskCreate, TaskUpdate, TaskList and TaskGet, but `update_plan` (desktop) is in neither the list nor the denylist. The reminder covers only the deferred case.

4. Progress narration
- Rule text: `user-messages.md:4` (acknowledgment allowed, "progress narration is not", "one short line at most"), `user-messages.md:10`, `task-list.md:3`, `requirements.md:10-12` (R-TASKLIST, R-ACK, R-NUDGE).
- Gap: "a brief acknowledgment" (`task-list.md:3`) has no length or content limit, so a status line can pass as an acknowledgment. The reminder (`session-reminder.md:6`) merges "acknowledge briefly" with "write only for decisions", which blurs the two.

5. Empty reply
- Rule text: `user-messages.md:8`, `task-list.md:3` ("after an empty reply, a harness demand for visible output gets one neutral line naming no hook"), `requirements.md:12` (R-NUDGE).
- Gap: the rule is conditional on a "harness demand" and never says what the root must do on an empty reply of its own. It is absent from the 5-bullet reminder (`session-reminder.md`). No hook can see an empty reply: the registered events are listed below, and none is a Stop hook.

6. Ready Assignments left unlaunched
- Rule text: `dispatch.md:9` ("Start all ready independent work together and end the turn"), `workflows.md:1` (`assignment create`, then `plan`, then write the script), `requirements.md:22` (R-DISPATCH).
- Gap: "end the turn" reads as permission to stop once work is started, and nothing says to launch Ready work the `plan` output names. `plan` returns `action: "none"` when `recommend` finds nothing (`overview.ts:111-112`). Workflows are off by default (`domain/directive.ts:15`, `workflowsAvailable: false`), so the workflow branch depends on configuration.

## Hook events registered (`packages/integrations/claude/src/generate.ts:126-150`; `dist/hooks/hooks.json`)

Five hook names on four events, six entries, each `timeout: 10`, exec form `bun … holyagent.js hook <name>`.

| Hook | Event and matcher | onFailure | What it may do (docs/hooks.md) |
|---|---|---|---|
| session-start | SessionStart `startup\|resume\|clear\|compact` | default | Context only. Capped at 9,300 chars (`sessioncontext.ts:10`; host cut at 10,000, per `docs/hooks.md:21`). Root core cap 4,100 (`sessioncontext.test.ts:39-44`) |
| subagent-start | SubagentStart (no matcher) | default | Context only (specialist rules) |
| vcs-reminder | PreToolUse Bash, `if Bash(*git*commit*)` and `Bash(*git*push*)` | default | Context only; never a decision |
| workflow | PreToolUse Workflow | block | Decision: allow an inline holyagent-only script (`hook.ts:347-371`); only `script` and `args` inputs (`hook.ts:190`) |
| agent-launch | PostToolUse Agent | default | Context only; records launches |

Exit 2 is the host's block; no hook uses it (`docs/hooks.md:3`). Failures print to stderr with exit 1 (`hook.ts:60-84`).

Events that could detect the failures (from the Claude Code hook reference as I know it; not checked against the host version in this session):
- Stop: empty reply (6), narration (4), ready work unlaunched (6). Input would be the stop-hook payload. Could block a stop, which would be the first enforcing hook. Verify schema on the host.
- UserPromptSubmit: could inject the reminder on each user message (3, 4).
- PreToolUse on Write, Edit, NotebookEdit: catches file tool writes but not Bash (1). A PreToolUse Bash `if` pattern for redirection or heredoc would cover Bash writes, though it is a guard, which `docs/hooks.md:75` says the maintainer removed on purpose.
- PreToolUse Agent or PostToolUse Workflow: could compare the last `plan` output with what launched (6, 7).
- SessionStart: can detect missing Intent (2) by reading `.holyagent`, which the current hook already does.

## Stdin on Windows (non-blocking claim)

Code: `main.ts:9-16` defines `stdin` as `Bun.stdin.text()` in `Effect.tryPromise`, lazily inside `Effect.suspend`. `main.ts:34` starts the whole run with `Effect.runFork`, and nothing awaits it. `context.ts:35-37` reads stdin only when a command has no `--input`.

Finding: the code gives no proof of loss. Nothing holds the fork's handle, and the process stays alive only while Bun's loop has an active handle. A pending pipe read on Windows may or may not keep the loop alive, and this could not be run, so the claim is unverified (inference). The in-process tests (`input.test.ts:136-145`, `cli.test.ts`) pass stdin as an Effect and never exercise `main.ts`, so this path has no test. CLAUDE.md says to call `Effect.runPromise` only at integration boundaries; `main.ts` uses `runFork` and sets `process.exitCode` in a tap. A fix belongs in `main.ts:34-48`: await the run with `Effect.runPromise` and set the exit code from its result.

## Failures 7 to 9 (workflow)

7. Plan says workflow, root ends the turn
- Rule text: `overview.ts:80-84` (PLAN_NOTES: "workflow first: … write the inline script yourself and run it with the Workflow tool"), `workflows.md:1-12`, `dispatch.md:9` ("end the turn").
- Gap: `workflows.md` never says "call the Workflow tool in this turn". `dispatch.md:9` says to end the turn, so the two read as a contradiction. The `plan` output (`overview.ts:113-141`) carries `action: "workflow"` but no "launch now" directive.

8. parallel() used where pipeline() fits
- Rule text: `workflows.md:5` ("run the Assignments through pipeline(), which has no barrier; use parallel() only where a stage needs every earlier result"), `overview.ts:81` ("Run the entries through pipeline()").
- Gap: `plan` prints `parallel: true` whenever more than one id is ready (`overview.ts:129`), and that field names the construct the rules say to avoid for independent work. Inference: this is the likely cause of the parallel() choice.
- The workflow checker allows both (`workflow-check.ts:50-51`, `:241-242`), so nothing blocks it.

9. Dispatch prompts retyped by hand
- Route today: `assignment dispatch` (`assignment.ts:165-205`) prints TOON fields, then `prompt:` and the prompt verbatim, on stdout. The root then types the prompt into the Workflow tool's `script` (a string literal in `agent()`) or into `args`. `hook.ts:190` allows only `script` and `args` in the call, and `workflow-check.ts:50-54` globals include `args`, which is plain data.
- Why retyping is unavoidable with this design: a workflow script has no file or process access (`workflow-check.ts`, host names such as `Bun`, `process`, `require`, `fetch` are refused), and the Workflow tool takes no file reference unless `scriptPath` or `name` is used. Both ask for permission (`hook.ts:347-371`; `docs/hooks.md:49`).
- Options for the CLI to offer (for the root to decide):
  a. `plan` prints a complete script with the prompts already embedded as literals, so the root copies one block, not composes it.
  b. Route prompts through `args`, which the hook already allows, so the literal text is data and not script code. The root still types it once.
  c. Have the workflow hook (PreToolUse Workflow, which can return a decision) add or rewrite inputs. Claude Code's `updatedInput` support is unverified here, so check the host reference first. This moves a trust boundary and needs the user's approval.
  d. Delegate writing to a writer: `builtinsOf` (`agents.ts:377-387`) gives Write to writing roles, so content can go to a Worker through an Assignment. The root still types the Assignment, so the saving is only in tokens for large content.
- Cost: a single copy per prompt is the floor under today's design. Option (c) is the only one that removes it.
